label: early original-phase first occurrence of l/z/1/a/q/n/s/k/p/b after e/3/t/o/u context
explanation: Fires only in the original input phase, at steps t=2..8 (peak t=3-4, none at t=0,1 or at delimiter/copy steps). Driven by the current input token: l is strongest (7.5x lift, 28% of mass, all top examples), then z, 1, a, q, n, s, k, p, b; almost never w or f. 95% of mass is on the first occurrence of the token. Magnitude is modulated by the prefix: it is largest when earlier inputs (especially the first token) are e, 3, t, o, u (first_tok e 5.4x, 3 4.1x; prev2_tok 3/e about 4.5x), e.g. e u 3 3 e [l]. Gate is graded: the same token/position conditions without the favorable prefix often stay below threshold, so precision is low (~0.19) though the predicate covers ~87% of activation mass on dev. Counting context tokens (n_seen>=2) raises precision only slightly and costs recall.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=3: l, 1, z, q; t=2: l, 1, z, a; t=4: l, 1, z, q) and the first original token (most: e, 3, t, u, o, d; least: 1, n, z, l); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=4, t=5.
